tasks.source_excerpt:
Alarm
Level 1 Abjuration (Ranger, Wizard)
Casting Time: 1 minute or Ritual
Range: 30 feet
Components: V, S, M (a bell and silver wire)
Duration: 8 hours
You set an alarm against intrusion. Choose a door,
a window, or an area within range that is no larger
than a 20-foot Cube. Until the spell ends, an alarm
alerts you whenever a creature touches or enters
the warded area. When you cast the spell, you can
designate creatures that won’t set off the alarm. You
also choose whether the alarm is audible or mental:
Audible Alarm. The alarm produces the sound of
a handbell for 10 seconds within 60 feet of the
warded area.
Mental Alarm. You are alerted by a mental ping
if you are within 1 mile of the warded area. This
ping awakens you if you’re asleep.

tasks.source_excerpt:
Commune with Nature
Level 5 Divination (Druid, Ranger)
Casting Time: 1 minute or Ritual
Range: Self
Components: V, S
Duration: Instantaneous
You commune with nature spirits and gain knowl-
edge of the surrounding area. In the outdoors, the
spell gives you knowledge of the area within 3 miles
of you. In caves and other natural underground
settings, the radius is limited to 300 feet. The spell
doesn’t function where nature has been replaced by
construction, such as in castles and settlements.
Choose three of the following facts; you learn
those facts as they pertain to the spell’s area:
• Locations of settlements
• Locations of portals to other planes of existence
• Location of one Challenge Rating 10+ creature
(GM’s choice) that is a Celestial, an Elemental, a
Fey, a Fiend, or an Undead
• The most prevalent kind of plant, mineral, or
Beast (you choose which to learn)
• Locations of bodies of water
For example, you could determine the location of a
powerful monster in the area, the locations of bod-
ies of water, and the locations of any towns.

Level 4 Enchantment (Druid, Ranger, Sorcerer)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 60 feet
Components: V, S
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
One Beast you can see within range must succeed
on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Charmed
condition for the duration. The target has Advan-
tage on the save if you or your allies are fighting it.
Whenever the target takes damage, it repeats the
save, ending the spell on itself on a success.
You have a telepathic link with the Charmed tar-
get while the two of you are on the same plane of
existence. On your turn, you can use this link to
issue commands to the target (no action required),

“Fetch that object.” The target does its best to obey
on its turn. If it completes an order and doesn’t re-
ceive further direction from you, it acts and moves
as it likes, focusing on protecting itself.
You can command the target to take a Reaction
but must take your own Reaction to do so.
Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. Your Concentra-
tion can last longer with a spell slot of level 5 (up to
10 minutes), 6 (up to 1 hour), or 7+ (up to 8 hours).

tasks.source_excerpt:
Elementalism
Transmutation Cantrip (Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 30 feet
Components: V, S
Duration: Instantaneous
You exert control over the elements, creating one of
the following effects within range.
Beckon Air. You create a breeze strong enough to
ripple cloth, stir dust, rustle leaves, and close open
doors and shutters, all in a 5-foot Cube. Doors and
shutters being held open by someone or something
aren’t affected.
Beckon Earth. You create a thin shroud of dust or
sand that covers surfaces in a 5-foot-square area, or
you cause a single word to appear in your handwrit-
ing in a patch of dirt or sand.
Beckon Fire. You create a thin cloud of harmless
embers and colored, scented smoke in a 5-foot Cube.
You choose the color and scent, and the embers can
light candles, torches, or lamps in that area. The
smoke’s scent lingers for 1 minute.
Beckon Water. You create a spray of cool mist that
lightly dampens creatures and objects in a 5-foot
Cube. Alternatively, you create 1 cup of clean water
either in an open container or on a surface, and the
water evaporates in 1 minute.
Sculpt Element. You cause dirt, sand, fire, smoke,
mist, or water that can fit in a 1-foot Cube to assume
a crude shape (such as that of a creature) for 1 hour.

Find Traps
Level 2 Divination (Cleric, Druid, Ranger)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 120 feet
Components: V, S
Duration: Instantaneous
You sense any trap within range that is within line
of sight. A trap, for the purpose of this spell, in-
cludes any object or mechanism that was created
to cause damage or other danger. Thus, the spell
would sense the Alarm or Glyph of Warding spell or a
mechanical pit trap, but it wouldn’t reveal a natural
weakness in the floor, an unstable ceiling, or a hid-
den sinkhole.

location. You do learn the general nature of the dan-
ger posed by a trap you sense.

Gust of Wind
Level 2 Evocation (Druid, Ranger, Sorcerer, Wizard)
Casting Time: Action
Range: Self
Components: V, S, M (a legume seed)
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
A Line of strong wind 60 feet long and 10 feet wide
blasts from you in a direction you choose for the
duration. Each creature in the Line must succeed on
a Strength saving throw or be pushed 15 feet away
from you in a direction following the Line. A crea-
ture that ends its turn in the Line must make the
same save.
Any creature in the Line must spend 2 feet of
movement for every 1 foot it moves when moving
closer to you.
The gust disperses gas or vapor, and it extin-
guishes candles and similar unprotected flames in
the area. It causes protected flames, such as those
of lanterns, to dance wildly and has a 50 percent
chance to extinguish them.
As a Bonus Action on your later turns, you can

change the direction in which the Line blasts from
you.

tasks.source_excerpt:
Meld into Stone
Level 3 Transmutation (Cleric, Druid, Ranger)
Casting Time: Action or Ritual
Range: Touch
Components: V, S
Duration: 8 hours
You step into a stone object or surface large enough
to fully contain your body, merging yourself and
your equipment with the stone for the duration.
You must touch the stone to do so. Nothing of your
presence remains visible or otherwise detectable by
nonmagical senses.
While merged with the stone, you can’t see what
occurs outside it, and any Wisdom (Perception)
checks you make to hear sounds outside it are made
with Disadvantage. You remain aware of the pas-
sage of time and can cast spells on yourself while
merged in the stone. You can use 5 feet of movement
to leave the stone where you entered it, which ends
the spell. You otherwise can’t move.
Minor physical damage to the stone doesn’t harm
you, but its partial destruction or a change in its
shape (to the extent that you no longer fit within it)
expels you and deals 6d6 Force damage to you. The
stone’s complete destruction (or transmutation into
a different substance) expels you and deals 50 Force
damage to you. If expelled, you move into an unoc-
cupied space closest to where you first entered and
have the Prone condition.

tasks.source_excerpt:
Plant Growth
Level 3 Transmutation (Bard, Druid, Ranger)
Casting Time: Action (Overgrowth) or
8 hours (Enrichment)
Range: 150 feet
Components: V, S
Duration: Instantaneous
This spell channels vitality into plants. The casting
time you use determines whether the spell has the
Overgrowth or the Enrichment effect below.
Overgrowth. Choose a point within range. All
normal plants in a 100-foot-radius Sphere centered
on that point become thick and overgrown. A crea-
ture moving through that area must spend 4 feet of
movement for every 1 foot it moves. You can exclude
one or more areas of any size within the spell’s area
from being affected.
Enrichment. All plants in a half-mile radius cen-
tered on a point within range become enriched for
365 days. The plants yield twice the normal amount
of food when harvested. They can benefit from only
one Plant Growth per year.

Plant Growth
Level 3 Transmutation (Bard, Druid, Ranger)
Casting Time: Action (Overgrowth) or
8 hours (Enrichment)
Range: 150 feet
Components: V, S
Duration: Instantaneous
This spell channels vitality into plants. The casting
time you use determines whether the spell has the
Overgrowth or the Enrichment effect below.
Overgrowth. Choose a point within range. All
normal plants in a 100-foot-radius Sphere centered
on that point become thick and overgrown. A crea-
ture moving through that area must spend 4 feet of
movement for every 1 foot it moves. You can exclude
one or more areas of any size within the spell’s area
from being affected.
Enrichment. All plants in a half-mile radius cen-
tered on a point within range become enriched for
365 days. The plants yield twice the normal amount
of food when harvested. They can benefit from only
one Plant Growth per year.

Speak with Plants
Level 3 Transmutation (Bard, Druid, Ranger)
Casting Time: Action
Range: Self
Components: V, S
Duration: 10 minutes
You imbue plants in an immobile 30-foot Emanation
with limited sentience and animation, giving them
the ability to communicate with you and follow your
simple commands. You can question plants about
events in the spell’s area within the past day, gain-
ing information about creatures that have passed,
weather, and other circumstances.
You can also turn Difficult Terrain caused by plant
growth (such as thickets and undergrowth) into
ordinary terrain that lasts for the duration. Or you
can turn ordinary terrain where plants are present
into Difficult Terrain that lasts for the duration.
The spell doesn’t enable plants to uproot them-
selves and move about, but they can move their
branches, tendrils, and stalks for you.
If a Plant creature is in the area, you can commu-
nicate with it as if you shared a common language.

tasks.source_excerpt:
Wind Wall
Level 3 Evocation (Druid, Ranger)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 120 feet
Components: V, S, M (a fan and a feather)
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
A wall of strong wind rises from the ground at a
point you choose within range. You can make the
wall up to 50 feet long, 15 feet high, and 1 foot
thick. You can shape the wall in any way you choose
so long as it makes one continuous path along the
ground. The wall lasts for the duration.
When the wall appears, each creature in its area
makes a Strength saving throw, taking 4d8 Blud-
geoning damage on a failed save or half as much
damage on a successful one.
The strong wind keeps fog, smoke, and other
gases at bay. Small or smaller flying creatures or
objects can’t pass through the wall. Loose, light-
weight materials brought into the wall fly upward.
Arrows, bolts, and other ordinary projectiles
launched at targets behind the wall are deflected
upward and miss automatically. Boulders hurled by
Giants or siege engines, and similar projectiles, are
unaffected. Creatures in gaseous form can’t pass
through it.

Level 3 Evocation (Druid, Ranger)

355.title: Dispel level-three-or-lower spells on one explicit creature
355.body:
<!-- edda-271:dispel-low -->

Parent: #193 · Decision: #271 · Roadmap: #47. One reviewable PR; L; afk. Implementation fixture; not full spell/family support.

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf), PDF pages 105, 106, 124, 179. SHA-256 `8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87`. Pin, attribution and adaptation: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`.

## Exact fixture

An isolated authorized level-five Cleric fixture uses level-three Dispel Magic on a known creature carrying Shield of Faith and Bless from independent casters.

## Targets

One known creature within 120 feet and clear path; end every qualifying ongoing spell on that target. A multi-recipient cast loses only the targeted recipient link, not other recipients.

## Costs

Magic action, one level-three slot, V/S. Automatic ending for ongoing spells level three or lower; no ability check for these spells.

## Timing and mechanic boundary

Commit action cost, exact affected spell/link IDs and history together. Distinguish ending the target’s spell effect from ending its caster’s unrelated concentration.

Proposed mechanic keys (planning identifiers, not registered support): `spell.dispel.creature.low-level`, `effect.remove.recipient-link`. Reconcile with #194/#277/#278; keep unknown keys unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test several qualifying spells, suppressed same-name effects, unrelated targets/casters, no eligible spells (legal cast still costs), reload and exact removal once.
- [ ] Reject unknown spell levels, level-four-or-higher effects and object/magical-effect targets with an explicit unsupported reason until the bounded follow-up decides them. Isolated authorized fixture only; production eligibility requires exact #323 advancement child, not decision closure.
- [ ] Durable mutation fixtures: lock/revalidate all involved actors and effect revisions; save costs, dice, effect/link state, clock/turn and history in one transaction. Inject history-write failure and prove complete rollback; retry same action ID returns the committed receipt with no extra roll, charge or effect. Reload/reconnect resumes exact identities and pending timing.
- [ ] Disclosure negatives: preview never rolls/writes; reject foreign campaign/actor IDs, hidden recipients and forged costs/timing; public receipts omit private NPC HP, unobserved spells and tactics. Unknown facts fail closed with an explicit reason. Preserve unrelated JSON and legacy reads.
- [ ] For higher-level isolated fixtures, demonstrate authoritative test entitlement explicitly; do not treat imported spell data or closing a class investigation as player eligibility. Publish any missing production-eligibility implementation prerequisite before enabling discovery.

## Hard prerequisites

- #203
- #352

Only these are hard prerequisites: source record/contract owners and the exact shared fixture named above. Class production eligibility stays unavailable where explicitly excluded. Every terminal implementation directly blocks both #279 and #280. A spike must add all of its resulting terminal implementation blockers to both gates before closure; decision closure supplies no playable evidence.

## Verification

`go test -short -race ./...` and `go vet ./...`. Runtime PRs must additionally run isolated PostgreSQL handler tests with `-tags=integration`, injectable dice, rollback, receipt replay and reload (short tests do not include them). Changed UI requires build/lint and desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect journeys. Spike PRs validate source/manifest and read back every published body, parent and dependency, checking acyclicity.

## Boundaries and exclusions

Start in `internal/rules/srd521`, `internal/game`, `internal/engine`, `internal/combat` and relevant handler fixtures. Keep the shared web/TUI action path; no production migration execution or deployment. No general antimagic, curses, nonspell magic-item removal, object/area targeting, higher-level checks/upcasting or automatic class advancement. No Full Rules claim. Retain CC-BY-4.0 attribution and mark adaptations. Close from the merged PR.

61.title: Resolve SRD checks and saving throws with inspectable dice receipts
61.body:
<!-- roadmap-slicer:edda-story-led-srd-521:issue:dice-checks -->
Use one deterministic rules path for supported ability checks/saves and expose the math in a character-sheet action fixture.

Epic: #50 Play supported SRD actions from the interactive sheet
Roadmap: #47 [Roadmap] Story-led Edda gameplay with SRD 5.2.1

**Delivery unit: one PR** (size M). Implement this outcome with its tests and docs. Do not absorb neighbouring issues; if it grows past one reviewable PR, split it and update the roadmap. An agent can finish this alone.

## Blocked by

- #58 Expose a typed rules-derived character sheet projection

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Injectable dice give source-based results for ordinary rolls, advantage/disadvantage, ability/proficiency and applicable expertise.
- [ ] The receipt records individual dice/modifiers and known outcome while filtering secret difficulties and hidden facts.
- [ ] Neither the language model nor React decides mechanical arithmetic.

## Verification

- `go test -short -race ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- For database changes, run `go test -tags integration -run Integration ./internal/handlers ./internal/state/sqlc` against isolated PostgreSQL.
- `pnpm --dir frontend build`
- `pnpm --dir frontend lint`
- Run the frontend behavior checks added under the regression-harness issue with isolated fixtures.

## Code boundaries

- internal/rules
- internal/game
- internal/tools
- pkg/api
- frontend/src/components/character

These are starting points, not a list of files to edit.

## Out of scope

- Attack/spell damage and expanding every situational feature.

## Notes

Use deterministic model doubles and injectable dice; no production accounts or paid inference are needed for mechanical checks. Preserve legacy campaign reads and the shared web/TUI engine boundary. One issue closes with one reviewable PR; do not absorb neighboring roadmap work.

353.title: End the exact concentration cast on resolved damage and incapacitation events
353.body:
<!-- edda-271:concentration-events -->

Parent: #193 · Decision: #271 · Roadmap: #47. One reviewable PR; M; afk. Implementation fixture; not full spell/family support.

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf), PDF pages 179, 184, 191. SHA-256 `8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87`. Pin, attribution and adaptation: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`.

## Exact fixture

A concentrating Cleric has two recorded independent damage sources, then a trusted Unconscious transition at positive HP; all recipient links end on failed save or incapacitation.

## Targets

The authoritative damaged/conditioned caster and only that caster’s effect recipients. Consume server-resolved events, never client-declared damage or condition flags.

## Costs

No action, spell slot, or recovery. One Constitution save per separate positive damage source while still concentrating; no save on incapacitation, death or zero-HP ending.

## Timing and mechanic boundary

Within the damage/condition transaction, before further use of the ended effect. DC min(30,max(10,floor(actual damage/2))). No check for zero damage or already-ended concentration.

Proposed mechanic keys (planning identifiers, not registered support): `concentration.damage.per-source`, `concentration.end.incapacitated`, `concentration.end.unconscious`, `concentration.end.dead`. Reconcile with #194/#277/#278; keep unknown keys unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test success/failure, odd half-damage rounding, cap 30, separate sources versus one damage instance, zero damage, positive-HP unconsciousness, incapacitation and death, and no resurrection of effects on healing/waking.
- [ ] Expose a narrow trusted event adapter with integration fixtures; #269 owns condition acquisition and all other condition consequences. Do not implement sleep spells, dying/death-save systems or general conditions here.
- [ ] Durable mutation fixtures: lock/revalidate all involved actors and effect revisions; save costs, dice, effect/link state, clock/turn and history in one transaction. Inject history-write failure and prove complete rollback; retry same action ID returns the committed receipt with no extra roll, charge or effect. Reload/reconnect resumes exact identities and pending timing.
- [ ] Disclosure negatives: preview never rolls/writes; reject foreign campaign/actor IDs, hidden recipients and forged costs/timing; public receipts omit private NPC HP, unobserved spells and tactics. Unknown facts fail closed with an explicit reason. Preserve unrelated JSON and legacy reads.
- [ ] For higher-level isolated fixtures, demonstrate authoritative test entitlement explicitly; do not treat imported spell data or closing a class investigation as player eligibility. Publish any missing production-eligibility implementation prerequisite before enabling discovery.

## Hard prerequisites

- #351

Only these are hard prerequisites: source record/contract owners and the exact shared fixture named above. Class production eligibility stays unavailable where explicitly excluded. Every terminal implementation directly blocks both #279 and #280. A spike must add all of its resulting terminal implementation blockers to both gates before closure; decision closure supplies no playable evidence.

## Verification

`go test -short -race ./...` and `go vet ./...`. Runtime PRs must additionally run isolated PostgreSQL handler tests with `-tags=integration`, injectable dice, rollback, receipt replay and reload (short tests do not include them). Changed UI requires build/lint and desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect journeys. Spike PRs validate source/manifest and read back every published body, parent and dependency, checking acyclicity.

## Boundaries and exclusions

Start in `internal/rules/srd521`, `internal/game`, `internal/engine`, `internal/combat` and relevant handler fixtures. Keep the shared web/TUI action path; no production migration execution or deployment. No duplicated #269 condition engine, #272 interrupted-rest flow, War Caster, concentration immunity or class exceptions. No Full Rules claim. Retain CC-BY-4.0 attribution and mark adaptations. Close from the merged PR.

774.title: Resolve shared Heroic Inspiration through immediate owned typed-die windows
774.body:
<!-- edda-325:heroic-inspiration -->
Parent #50; decision #325; roadmap #47. One PR. Task Size L.

Required native path: this terminal -> #728 -> #337.

Pinned SRD5.2.1 PDF47–49 and explicitly cited consumed rules. SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md. Fixture/ownership decisions are Edda additions.

Scope and deterministic positive/negative fixtures: PDF183 Heroic Inspiration; Champion grant PDF49, Human Resourceful remains #333. One shared durable PC-held boolean pool, maximum one; generic receipt/provenance with NO automatic gains. Immediately after rolling ANY owned known typed die, may expend held Heroic Inspiration to reroll that single die and MUST use new face even when worse. Not only d20, not entire dice pool, not a later arbitrary history reroll. Deterministic bounded positive/negative adapters are mandatory for current shared-engine ability-check/saving-throw d20, weapon attack d20 and individual weapon-damage d8, existing healing dice, Fighter advancement d10/fixed-choice rejection, and individually typed feat/resource dice when their exact effect owner is qualified. Each die role names its existing resolver and immediate phase; keep unsupported/unregistered adapters unavailable. Preserve original face, chosen die identity, replacement face, final dependent outcome and source provenance; one immediate window, explicit use/decline, no intervening roll/action, immutable original receipt plus final replacement reconciliation. Source gain producers remain separate: Champion751 can grant ONLY during combat at start of own turn without it; Human Resourceful is owned by333, never enabled here. If a NEW gain arrives while already held, it is lost unless explicitly given to a PC who lacks it; transfer this new gain only, no stockpiling or invented transfer of previously held inspiration, no recursive duplicate gain. Overflow transfer requires known owned/authorized PC context, never foreign/NPC/hidden actors or private roll disclosures. Stable action/roll/gain IDs bind pool cost, die replacement, dependent effects and history atomically; reload/concurrent use applies once, all injected failure paths roll back cost/dice/effect/history. Bardic Inspiration512 remains a different resource and is not reused. No species/class eligibility or spell work. All feature/admission consumers require qualified typed adapter; generic pool presence does not qualify every roll. Parent50; exact native prerequisites61/64/65. Shared qualification paths: this terminal->279 and280; this terminal->751->728->337 and directly->728->337. Positive: a known owned ability-check die with secret DC and undisclosed outcome opens the immediate Heroic Inspiration use/decline window; a worse reroll must be kept, while the DC and outcome remain undisclosed. Negative: that same unknown outcome cannot open Tactical Mind or Indomitable, and hidden/foreign dice, stale windows and unregistered adapters cannot open Heroic Inspiration.

For each exact predicate below: deterministic positive and independently violated negative fixtures, unsupported/forged origin/level/owner rejection, inert prepare/cancel with no dice/state/history changes, explicit confirmed choice, stale revision rejection, stable action-ID replay after lost response and durable reload, concurrent confirmation applies once, atomic cost/dice/history/database rollback including injected write failures, no private DC/hidden target/lore disclosure. Shared engine through web AND trusted TUI: disabled/unavailable explanations, confirmation/cancel/reconnect/retry and keyboard/phone journeys. Injectable dice unit tests plus isolated PostgreSQL handler/state integration tests; frontend build/changed-file lint/behavior fixtures and TUI command tests. GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and GOMAXPROCS=2 go vet -p 2 ./... . Feature tests use isolated entitlements; only separately qualified admission/transition may grant them. Unknown outcomes never imply success/failure. Outcome-dependent reactions such as Tactical Mind and Indomitable require a disclosed qualifying outcome. Heroic Inspiration remains available immediately after an owned known die even when the DC and outcome are undisclosed. Deliver readable story-led play, an interactive rules-backed character sheet, grounded action assistance and faithful chapters across desktop and phone, while keeping the main gameplay screen within one viewport like the current app.

## How to use this roadmap

This roadmap and its epics are tracking issues, not implementation PRs. Each work issue is **one reviewable PR**, and native GitHub dependencies set the order: an issue is ready when every issue it depends on is closed. Close a work issue from its merged PR with `Closes #<n>`. Tracking issues depend on their children, so they close last.

Plan: [Detailed product and implementation plan](https://github.com/subculture-collective/edda/blob/c2beafa55ff18b8d880096dcba56914a6870ed29/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-14-story-led-rules-gameplay.md), source commit `c2beafa`. The plan defines the complete target; work below is split into reviewable PRs and bounded investigations.

## Decisions

- SRD 5.2.1 is the pinned rules reference; use one authoritative server rules/action path.
- Story-led play; interactive sheet with targets/options/costs; rolls happen on confirmation with inspectable results.
- Narrative combat with initiative, explicit range/conditions and target selection; no required grid UI.
- Main gameplay fits one viewport on desktop and phone, with internal transcript/detail scrolling and anchored reachable action controls.
- Preserve the current Art Deco design language and the overall choice-based campaign creation process.
- Ghost text accepts with Tab or touch into an editable draft; accepting a suggestion never submits it.
- Faithful chapters follow played outcomes without invented events or hidden lore.

## Epics

- [ ] #48 Make campaign actions private, durable and recoverable: 12 PR(s). Reuse the review findings to protect campaign ownership, action order, persistence and client recovery.

- [ ] #50 Play supported SRD actions from the interactive sheet: 13 PR(s). Deliver small vertical slices for skills, attacks, items, narrative combat and casting.

- [x] #53 Read and export faithful campaign chapters: 4 PR(s). Turn committed player-visible play into durable chapters with a reader, source links and fidelity checks.

[Candidate evidence](https://github.com/subculture-collective/edda/blob/d103c0b/docs/playtest/issue-89/README.md) is in draft PR #343. Whole-tree frontend lint retains 22 baseline errors. These are separate component/contract fixtures, not a single continuous real-browser/real-database campaign or a production deployment.

The candidate fixes explicit same-action recovery after a server error, with campaign ID isolation and optimistic-entry/history reconciliation. It intentionally leaves #89 open: the fresh Android attempt again hit DEVICE_IN_USE owned by another session, and a final human player-experience review is not recorded. #46/#78 remain open.

Real PostgreSQL evidence also exposes the SRD free-text gap: typed actions succeed, but ordinary text reaches the intentional legacy guard. #342 is a bounded implementation under #50, with prerequisites #64/#88, Size L, and a native blocker of #89. It prepares only `Make an Athletics check` through the authoritative preview/explicit-confirm path; arbitrary text and legacy mutations stay unavailable. Independent implementation is proceeding in a separate PR; no unsupported pass is claimed here.

353.title: End the exact concentration cast on resolved damage and incapacitation events
353.body:
<!-- edda-271:concentration-events -->

Parent: #193 · Decision: #271 · Roadmap: #47. One reviewable PR; M; afk. Implementation fixture; not full spell/family support.

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf), PDF pages 179, 184, 191. SHA-256 `8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87`. Pin, attribution and adaptation: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`.

## Exact fixture

A concentrating Cleric has two recorded independent damage sources, then a trusted Unconscious transition at positive HP; all recipient links end on failed save or incapacitation.

## Targets

The authoritative damaged/conditioned caster and only that caster’s effect recipients. Consume server-resolved events, never client-declared damage or condition flags.

## Costs

No action, spell slot, or recovery. One Constitution save per separate positive damage source while still concentrating; no save on incapacitation, death or zero-HP ending.

## Timing and mechanic boundary

Within the damage/condition transaction, before further use of the ended effect. DC min(30,max(10,floor(actual damage/2))). No check for zero damage or already-ended concentration.

Proposed mechanic keys (planning identifiers, not registered support): `concentration.damage.per-source`, `concentration.end.incapacitated`, `concentration.end.unconscious`, `concentration.end.dead`. Reconcile with #194/#277/#278; keep unknown keys unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test success/failure, odd half-damage rounding, cap 30, separate sources versus one damage instance, zero damage, positive-HP unconsciousness, incapacitation and death, and no resurrection of effects on healing/waking.
- [ ] Expose a narrow trusted event adapter with integration fixtures; #269 owns condition acquisition and all other condition consequences. Do not implement sleep spells, dying/death-save systems or general conditions here.
- [ ] Durable mutation fixtures: lock/revalidate all involved actors and effect revisions; save costs, dice, effect/link state, clock/turn and history in one transaction. Inject history-write failure and prove complete rollback; retry same action ID returns the committed receipt with no extra roll, charge or effect. Reload/reconnect resumes exact identities and pending timing.
- [ ] Disclosure negatives: preview never rolls/writes; reject foreign campaign/actor IDs, hidden recipients and forged costs/timing; public receipts omit private NPC HP, unobserved spells and tactics. Unknown facts fail closed with an explicit reason. Preserve unrelated JSON and legacy reads.
- [ ] For higher-level isolated fixtures, demonstrate authoritative test entitlement explicitly; do not treat imported spell data or closing a class investigation as player eligibility. Publish any missing production-eligibility implementation prerequisite before enabling discovery.

## Hard prerequisites

- #351

Only these are hard prerequisites: source record/contract owners and the exact shared fixture named above. Class production eligibility stays unavailable where explicitly excluded. Every terminal implementation directly blocks both #279 and #280. A spike must add all of its resulting terminal implementation blockers to both gates before closure; decision closure supplies no playable evidence.

## Verification

`go test -short -race ./...` and `go vet ./...`. Runtime PRs must additionally run isolated PostgreSQL handler tests with `-tags=integration`, injectable dice, rollback, receipt replay and reload (short tests do not include them). Changed UI requires build/lint and desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect journeys. Spike PRs validate source/manifest and read back every published body, parent and dependency, checking acyclicity.

## Boundaries and exclusions

Start in `internal/rules/srd521`, `internal/game`, `internal/engine`, `internal/combat` and relevant handler fixtures. Keep the shared web/TUI action path; no production migration execution or deployment. No duplicated #269 condition engine, #272 interrupted-rest flow, War Caster, concentration immunity or class exceptions. No Full Rules claim. Retain CC-BY-4.0 attribution and mark adaptations. Close from the merged PR.

429.title: Confirm one source-linked D12 level and derived-stat transition
429.body:
<!-- edda-321:advancement -->
Parent: #336; decision #321; roadmap #47; blocks #498; #498 directly blocks #337.

Delivery: one reviewable PR, Task Size M.

Source: pinned English SRD5.2.1 pp28-30 and explicitly named referenced pages below; SHA256 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution and adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md.

Scope and deterministic positive fixture: PDF p23: validate earned XP against exact 20-row advancement source, add one D12 Hit Die, choose roll 1d12 or fixed 7 + CON, minimum gain1; recompute PB by total character level and all derived values. CON modifier changes adjust maximum HP for every attained character level exactly once. No automatic healing, feature effects, class eligibility or arbitrary level jumps. Reusable transaction consumed by each named transition.

Negative fixtures: violate each stated eligibility/number/target/action/resource/timing predicate independently; reject unsupported variants and forged levels. Preview and cancellation never mutate.

Required acceptance: Authoritative campaign/actor/source/rules-version/class-level eligibility; isolated high-level test entitlements grant no production access. Prepare previews costs/choices/targets/timing without dice or writes; explicit confirm revalidates current revision and commits choices, injectable dice, resource/action costs, effects, derived sheet and public history atomically. Store durable action receipt: same-ID retry/reload/reconnect returns exact committed result with no reroll/recharge/regrant; conflicting payload or concurrent stale confirmation rejected; two concurrent confirmations spend/apply once. Inject history/effect/choice failure and prove full PostgreSQL rollback. Protect private NPC HP, hidden actors, tactics and private choices in discovery/preview/history/error/reconnect. Shared web/TUI availability, disabled reason, accessible confirmation/cancel and reconnect fixtures required; desktop/phone confirmation journeys for changed web UI. Unknown prerequisites fail closed. Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p2 -short -race ./... and go vet -p2 ./...; isolated PostgreSQL integration rollback/replay/reload/concurrency tests; frontend build, changed-file lint and behavior fixtures when UI changes. Preserve legacy reads/unrelated JSON; retain CC-BY-4.0 attribution and adaptations. No production deployment, inference or broad coverage promotion.

Ownership: feature resolvers own behavior; level/entry applications consume them and apply grants once. Feature tests use explicit isolated entitlements, never grant production class admission. Data and earlier levels never unlock broader support. Shared #272 rests, #273 casting, #333 origins, #335 multiclass, #336 advancement, #384 selection/#389 ability updater, #269/#270 conditions and #278 equipment retain their scopes. Exact shared terminals in this matrix must block #498 natively; #498 blocks #337. Planning closure is insufficient. Selected feat effect must have its own terminal gate before admission; never implement spell/item effects here. No child implementation or qualification is supplied by this decision.

Native blocked-by: #285, #286, #308, #336.

779.title: Confirm player Unarmed Strike damage Grapple or Shove
779.body:
<!-- edda-326:unarmed -->
Parent: #50; decision #326; Task Size M; roadmap #47.

One reviewable PR. Source: SRD5.2.1 PDF49-52 and exact named clauses below. Pin 8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87. CC-BY-4.0 attribution/adaptation: docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md; fixture/ownership boundaries are Edda additions.

Scope and source-bound positive/negative deterministic fixtures: PDF190: within5ft choose damage (STR+PB attack,1+STR Bludgeoning), Grapple or Shove (target chooses STR/DEX save versus8+STR+PB). Grapple needs free hand, at most one size larger; Shove same size limit, choose push5ft or Prone. Positive: failed save pushes5; negative: oversized target, occupied hand, guessed hidden target, or swapping save after result fails.

For this one PR, preview is inert; explicit confirmation revalidates authoritative eligibility, source/version, target facts and expected revision. Persist choice, exact dice, once-only cost/use and history atomically. Receipt replay/retry/reload returns the same result without rerolling or charging again. Inject history failure for full rollback; race two confirmations and require one commit; stale/foreign/unsupported state rejects without mutation. Prove this with deterministic dice and isolated PostgreSQL handler/state fixtures. Disclose only player-known targets, choices, costs and source derivations; hidden/foreign facts never enter previews, receipts or errors. Shared engine serves web and TUI: explicitly expose supported choices or show unavailable with a reason on both; require desktop/phone confirmation and reconnect plus TUI behavior fixtures before availability. No Full Rules/coverage promotion. Higher-level isolated fixture state never grants production entitlement. Run GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and go vet -p 2 ./...; changed UI requires build, focused lint and behavior tests. Prepare performs no dice rolls or writes; cancellation is inert. Confirmation atomically commits action/resource costs, dice, target/effect state, derived sheet and history with one durable receipt.

Feature execution uses isolated entitlements, never production class admission. Class applications consume implemented contracts and grant once. Unknown origin/multiclass/feat/variant fails closed. #58 sheet; #61 dice; #64 confirmation; #65 martial actions; #67 trusted targets; #427/#428 completed rests; #429 XP/PB/CON transaction with distinct Monk D8/fixed5 adapter; #430 provenance only. #333/#335/#336 retain planning scopes. No runtime, grants, derived bonuses, coverage, deployment or Full Rules promotion in decision326.
